predecessors.name: French Mandate for Syria and the Lebanon
predecessors.text: Syria as the mandate left it after Lebanon was separated: independence 'attained on 24 October 1945' and the last French troops out on 17 April 1946

successors.name: United Arab Republic
successors.text: Syria as the Northern region of the union with Egypt announced on 1 February 1958; infobox formation 22 February 1958

ledger.x: 17 April 1946: Syria's independence, with the last French troops gone.
ledger.cpn: French Mandate for Syria and the Lebanon

ledger.x: 10 June 1948: Syrian forces hold Mishmar HaYarden.
20 July 1949: Syria and Israel sign the armistice, ending the fighting on the Syrian front; Israel had signed with Egypt on 24 February, Lebanon on 23 March and Jordan on 3 April.
1 February 1958: Syria and Egypt announce their union as the United Arab Republic.

wars.name: 1948 Arab-Israeli War (Syrian front)
wars.outcome: Syria invaded on 15 May 1948, took Samakh (18 May) and left it, attacked Degania (20 May), overran Mishmar HaYarden (10 June) and was 'stopped just west of the original border between Palestine and Syria'; the Syrians 'remained in the area until the 1949…

certainty.note: Frontiers inherited from the mandate; the eastern desert frontier is approximate and the Sanjak of Alexandretta, lost to Turkey in 1939, was never recognised.

The Israeli frontier is the armistice line of 20 July 1949, a line along the international border with demilitarised zones; the eastern desert frontier with Iraq and Jordan stays approximate and Hatay is still claimed.
